newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Nomura remains bullish on Cofinec.
newsitem.headline: Nomura remains bullish on Cofinec.

text.p: French packaging company Cofinec, the only foreign firm listed on the Budapest bourse, is set to rebound from recent falls after changes in its top management, Nomura Equity Research said.

"With the resignation of managing director Stephen Frater and the appointment of a new CEO from Tetra-Pak, the stage is set for a rapid renaissance at Cofinec," analysts Frances Cloud and Matthew Arnold said in a company update.
They rated Cofinec shares as a "buy." @
After releasing below expectations first half results, Cofinec responded to shareholder pressure by removing its managing director Stephen Frater on September 9.

The move followed an almost continuous fall of Cofinec price on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) from around 6,000 forints before the first half figures were released to an all-time low of 3,840 forints on September 6.
On Tuesday Cofinec closed at 4,200 forints, down 300, on the BSE. @

Nomura praised Frater's replacement by supervisory board chairman Pehr Gyllenhammer but said the appointment of Carlos Barbero from Tetra-Pak as CEO was more important because he will bring industrial experience at top management level.

"Mr Barbero should bring some much-needed industrial expertise into Cofinec, which - one would hope - will be built on by the managing director who will be brought in to follow Mr Gyllenhammer," the analysts said. @

Nomura attributed Cofinec's problems to lack of industrial experience at the level of top management and not from a true failure, either of the businesses themselves or of the concept of packaging in central Europe.
"For this reason, we are not altering our forecasts except to incorporate the announced restructuring provisions," they said.

"While there clearly remains some risk that legal action will be taken against the company, we are confident that with a stronger management team in place at the top, Cofinec should be able to show strong earnings growth from 1997 onwards." @
